title: Psalm 29 (Septuagint) = Psalm 30 (KJV)
description: Psalm 29 in the Septuagint numbering (Psalm 30 in the KJV). Both the manuscript page scan AND the Greek text are taken directly from Codex Sinaiticus (4th century AD) via the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). The Greek transcription preserves the actual uncial forms, lunate sigma, nomina sacra abbreviations, and lectional marks of the manuscript. Library folio: 94. English translation verbatim from the King James Version (1611, public domain) via bible-api.com.
introduction:
This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library, with the manuscript text drawn directly from the same source as the scan:

  1. Manuscript scan: The actual folio of Codex Sinaiticus containing this passage, from the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). Library folio reference: 94.
  2. Original text: The verbatim transcription of the Sinaiticus manuscript from the Codex Sinaiticus Project, preserving uncial forms, lunate sigma, nomina sacra (e.g. ⟨θϲ⟩ = θεός), and scribal marks. Nomina sacra are shown in angle brackets to indicate the manuscript's sacred-name abbreviations.
  3. English translation: The King James Version (1611), retrieved verbatim from the public-domain bible-api.com endpoint.

Numbering: Codex Sinaiticus follows the Septuagint Psalter, in which this is Psalm 29. In the Hebrew and King James numbering the same psalm is Psalm 30. Greek verse numbers follow the Septuagint, which counts the superscription as verse 1; English verse numbers follow the KJV, so they run 1 behind the Greek. The Greek and English in each section are the same words of the same psalm.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>ψαλμοϲ τωδηϲ του εγʼκαινιϲμου του οικου τω δαυειδʼ <sup>2</sup>υψωϲω ϲε κε οτι ϋπελαβεϲ με και ουκ ευφραναϲ τουϲ εχθρουϲ μου επ εμοι <sup>3</sup>κε ο θϲ μου εκεκραξα προϲ ϲε και ϊαϲω με <sup>4</sup>κε ανηγαγεϲ εξ αδου την ψυχην μου εϲωϲαϲ με εκ των καταβαινοντων ειϲ λακκον <sup>5</sup>ψαλατε τω κω οι οϲιοι αυτου και εξομολογειϲθε τη μνημη τηϲ αγιωϲυνηϲ αυτου
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>I will extol thee, O LORD; for thou hast lifted me up, and hast not made my foes to rejoice over me. <sup>2</sup>O LORD my God, I cried unto thee, and thou hast healed me. <sup>3</sup>O LORD, thou hast brought up my soul from the grave: thou hast kept me alive, that I should not go down to the pit. <sup>4</sup>Sing unto the LORD, O ye saints of his, and give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness.

translation.original_text: <sup>6</sup>οτι οργη εν τω θυμω αυτου και ζωη ε τω θεληματι αυτου το εϲπεραϲ αυλιϲθηϲεται κλαυθμοϲ και ειϲ το πρωϊ αγαλλιαϲιϲ <sup>7</sup>εγω δε ειπα εν τη ευθηνια μου ου μη ϲαλευθω ειϲ τον αιωνα <sup>8</sup>κε εν τω θεληματι ϲου παραϲχου τω καλλι μου δυναμιν απεϲτρεψαϲ δε το προϲωπον ϲου και εγενηθην τεταραγμενοϲ <sup>9</sup>προϲ ϲε κε κεκραξομαι και προϲ τον θν μου δεηθηϲομαι <sup>10</sup>τιϲ ωφελεια εν τω αιματι μου εν τω καταβηναι με ειϲ διαφθοραν μη εξομολογηϲεται ϲοι χουϲ η αναγγελει την αληθειαν ϲου
translation.text:
<sup>5</sup>For his anger
endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy
cometh in the morning. <sup>6</sup>And in my prosperity I said, I shall never be moved. <sup>7</sup>LORD, by thy favour thou hast made my mountain to stand strong: thou didst hide thy face,
and I was troubled. <sup>8</sup>I cried to thee, O LORD; and unto the LORD I made supplication. <sup>9</sup>What profit
is there in my blood, when I go down to the pit? Shall the dust praise thee? shall it declare thy truth?

translation.original_text: <sup>11</sup>ηκουϲεν κϲ και ηλεηϲεν με κϲ εγενηθη βοηθοϲ μου <sup>12</sup>εϲτρεψαϲ τον κοπετον μου ειϲ χαραν εμοι διερρηξαϲ τον ϲακκον μου και περιεζωϲαϲ με ευφροϲυνην <sup>13</sup>οπωϲ αν ψαλη ϲοι η δοξα μου και ου μη κατανυγω κε ο θϲ μου ειϲ τον αιωνα εξομολογηϲομαι ϲοι
translation.text:
<sup>10</sup>Hear, O LORD, and have mercy upon me: LORD, be thou my helper. <sup>11</sup>Thou hast turned for me my mourning into dancing: thou hast put off my sackcloth, and girded me with gladness; <sup>12</sup>To the end that
my glory may sing praise to thee, and not be silent. O LORD my God, I will give thanks unto thee for ever.

verification.section_folios_note: Each section links to the specific folio(s) containing its verses, resolved per verse via the Codex Sinaiticus Project page index.
